evidence_quotes.quote: Water is very expensive as it costs 1000 shillings (0.4 USD) from the water vendors
water sources are also at a flat rate with no consideration
Water sources are very far. I walk for a distance of 12km

rationale: This qualitative study (6 focus group discussions with 49 people living with HIV/AIDS and 12 key informant interviews in Mpigi and Gomba districts, Uganda, analyzed via qualitative content analysis) investigates barriers to WASH access among PLWHA. Among rule-type mechanisms, user fees, vendor pricing, and flat-rate tariff structures without pro-poor social tariffs or subsidies at boreholes, water points, and public latrines clearly dominate (`fees_tariffs_subsidies`), alongside secondary mentions of the absence of special institutional accommodations/exemptions (`discretion_accommodation`) and non-participation of PLWHA in water user and sanitary management committees (`participation_assistance`). On the outcome side, both `effective_access` (reliance on contaminated surface-water ponds/lakes, water quality/treatment acceptability, insufficient water quantity, 12 km fetching burden, and physically unsuitable latrines for sick users) and `economic_access` (household inability to afford per-jerrican borehole/vendor fees, per-use public latrine charges, soap, and storage vessels) are co-equally central empirical findings (`multiple`, with `effective_access` as primary).
